COUNTRY: Saudi Arabia applied whole-project, supported by both paper and EBI title/description. HOST: human applied whole-project (hospital patients). ISOLATION_SOURCE: genuinely mixed (blood, urine, wound/sputum); no single source reaches ~95%. COLLECTION_DATE: 8-year span (2014–2022) exceeds the 2-year threshold; not backfilled.

notes: Sizing: ENA holds 508 Kp samples; paper describes 509 Kp isolates — near-complete match (one isolate may have been excluded during ENA deposition or Kleborate filtering). The EBI study title references 'Methylation analysis… PacBio sequencing', which is discordant with the paper's Illumina HiSeq methodology; PacBio likely refers to a subset analysis not described in this paper, but sample counts confirm this is the primary associated publication. Study setting is mixed: 459 hospital clinical + 9 hospital-sourced wastewater (hospital) vs 41 veterinary clinic isolates (community per rubric); veterinary arm is a deliberate second-setting inclusion. AMR study is surveillance: the collection is explicitly described as a convenience sample with no AMR phenotype/genotype gate for inclusion; ~78% of isolates lacked carbapenemases and 75% were susceptible to imipenem, confirming non-AMR-selected collection. Cohort age: no patient age data reported anywhere in the paper. Isolation source not backfilled due to genuine source diversity (blood 32%, urine 31%, rectal swab 10%, pus 7%, wastewater 7%, veterinary). Host not applied whole-project because veterinary (n=41) and wastewater (n=9) samples (~10%) fall below the ~95% threshold needed for whole-project human assignment; 'human' is still the predominant proposed value. Collection date spans 1980–2019 (39 years), well above the 5-year cap for date backfill.

notes: ENA total 285 samples, paper describes 281 analyzed isolates (294 collected minus 13 excluded for quality) — close match consistent with single-accession study. AMR selection was a cascade: AST flag (ESBL/ertapenem MIC) → phenotypic carbapenemase test → blaKPC PCR; all 281 deposited isolates confirmed blaKPC-positive by PCR, making PCR the definitive selection gate. study_setting.evidence_quote: A total of 168 non-redundant clinical strains of K. pneumoniae were collected from January 2015 to April 2018 by MIROKU Medical Laboratory, Hiroshima University and Nagoya University Hospital, all located in Japan. Among them, 85 strains were isolated from blood, 37 from respiratory tract (29 from sputum, five from nasopharyngeal swab, two from tracheal aspirate, one from bronchoalveolar lavage), 24 from urine (12 from urinary catheter, ten from midstream urine and two from non-classified urine samples), two from pus, one from skin and one from bile.
